subject: Intermittent inference latency — root analysis and customer assurance plan
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finmech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent latency impacting inference — seeing 500-800ms p95 for several routes

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in inference latency around 08:00 PDT and it’s persisted intermittently. Our dashboards show p95 jumping from ~120ms to 500–800ms for requests routed to the us-west cluster; a few requests also returned 502s. This is affecting our UI load times and a small percentage of downstream recommendations.

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood’s side or our client configuration? We can share traces and request ids — attaching two examples.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Platform Engineering, FinMech

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@finmech.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-21T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: root analysis, timeline, and corrective actions (FinMech)

Sarah — following our call earlier today, please find the post-incident summary and customer-facing RCA. I’ve included a concise timeline, the root analysis, immediate mitigations we applied, and our medium-term action commitments. The full technical appendix is attached (redwood_rca_finmech_20280821.pdf).

Executive summary:
- What happened: Between 07:58–09:42 PDT on 2028-08-18, a subset of inference requests routed to the us-west serving pool experienced elevated queuing latency leading to p95 increases (500–800ms) and intermittent 502 errors. Impacted endpoints: /v1/generate and /v1/chat for model variants rwd-small-1, rwd-medium-2.
- Customer impact: about 2.3% of your requests saw latency beyond your SLO during the window; 0.04% returned 5xx.
- Primary cause: a regression in a recent autoscaling heuristic combined with a kernel placement decision that caused uneven GPU slot allocation across hosts under a transient workload burst. This increased queueing on a subset of nodes.

Timeline (short):
- 2028-08-18 07:58 PDT — first latency alert from internal monitors (us-west cluster).
- 2028-08-18 08:00 PDT — FinMech dashboard anomalies reported (Sarah).
- 2028-08-18 08:06 PDT — triage begun; initial hypothesis: transient load spike.
- 2028-08-18 08:18 PDT — SRE observed high queue depth on hosts gpu-usw-12..14.
- 2028-08-18 08:27 PDT — temporary routing shift applied to distribute requests away from affected hosts; p95 began to stabilize.
- 2028-08-18 09:10 PDT — mitigation: rollback of autoscaler heuristic patch that had shipped 2028-08-17 22:45 PDT.
- 2028-08-18 09:42 PDT — metrics returned to baseline across all routes.

Root cause details (concise):
- A change to the autoscaler’s burst-handling heuristic intended to reduce overscaling had an unintended side effect: under certain short-lived bursts the scheduler delayed spinning up additional worker slots and instead concentrated new requests on already-provisioned hosts.
- Simultaneously, a recent kernel selector optimization preferred a lower-latency kernel on some hosts that reduced per-request throughput for larger-context requests. The combination increased queueing on a small host subset.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled back the autoscaler heuristic (complete at 09:10 PDT).
- Forced redistribution of traffic via control-plane routing rules at 08:27 PDT to avoid impacted hosts.
- Added a short-term autoscaler cooldown adjustment to prevent repeated oscillation.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Engineering: Add a regression test that simulates short burst patterns to the autoscaler CI. Owner: Hannah Schmitt — ETA 2028-09-05.
- Serving runtime: Re-evaluate kernel-selector logic for large-context requests; implement a fallback threshold. Owner: Jonas Weber — ETA 2028-09-12.
- Platform: Add an SLO-aligned control that triggers faster warm-up under bursty signals. Owner: Irene Choi — ETA 2028-08-30 (hotfix), broader rollout by 2028-09-20.
- Customer-facing: Provide request-level verification package (logs + request ids) for your team. Owner: Marissa Cole — ETA 2028-08-22.

Verification steps for FinMech:
- We attached the anonymized request ids that exhibited 5xxs and high latency — you can correlate against your traces.
- We’ll run a joint validation test (small controlled burst) with your team next week; proposed window: 2028-08-24 10:00 PDT. Please confirm availability.

Compensation: Per our incident credit policy and the impact window above, we will apply service credits to your August invoice. If you prefer an alternative form of remediation (e.g., fwd capacity), let me know and I’ll route for approvals.

Attachments: redwood_rca_finmech_20280821.pdf (technical appendix), latency_event_log_0818.csv (submitted by FinMech).

We deeply regret the disruption. Our engineering teams have prioritized the follow-ups above; we’ll share progress updates in this thread.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_rca_finmech_20280821.pdf, type: application/pdf)
